newsitem.title: UK: Copper continues consolidation, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Copper continues consolidation, others mixed.

text.p: Copper prices fluctuated widely on Thursday as the market attempted to consolidate after the past few week's gains.

Metals market sentiment took an early blow from overnight news that Lehman Brothers is to wind down its metals and energy business and relinquish LME broker status and this brought a few selling orders into a thin and nervous market.
This put copper quickly down to the bottom end of its range but when support held at $2,185, the price rallied back to $2,216, and some buying flowed back into all metals.
The market subsequently remained between these levels before last business at $2,212, down $3 from Wednesday.
Market talk ahead of Friday's LME stocks release was indecisive but the opinion seemed to be spreading that the downtrend may be nearly over.
Aluminium twice dipped to $1,500 during the day after failing to break resistance at $1,520. But the downside held and last business was at $1,504, down $4 a tonne.
Zinc succumbed to a bout of profittaking after the $1,085 resistance level had successfully repelled a bout of early buying prompted by news Anvil Range is to shut its Yukon lead/zinc mine.
Three months zinc last traded at $1,076, down one.
But lead held firm, setting new high for the day at $714 before last business at $713, up $9 from Wednesday.
Nickel drifted back from the morning's highs but still ended $20 up on the day and dealers said that its recent setback had brought in consumer buying which had prompted shortcvoering.
At one stage in the morning nickel had reached $6,960.

Traders noted news that German steel producers aassociation WVS said local nickel consumption was down 15,000 to 18,000 tonnes in 1996. But they were encouraged by an expected three to five percent rise in stainless steel production in 1997.
Tin staged an encouraging technical performance, according to some traders, and by the close was eroding resistance near $6,150. It last traded at $6,160, up $70.
Alloy ended at $1,345/$1,350, down $5 a tonne.
